events.title: Commodore PET 2001 released
events.summary: Commodore introduced the PET 2001 in January 1977 — one of the first complete personal computers with built-in monitor, keyboard, and cassette storage.
events.about: The PET shipped with Microsoft BASIC in ROM and a chiclet keyboard in an all-in-one case — no soldering required. Schools and small businesses used it for accounting and teaching programming before the Apple II and TRS-80 defined the home PC market. Commodore's vertical integration foreshadowed the C64 price wars to come.

narrative.whyChosen: The PET 2001 was among the first ready-to-use personal computers sold to the public.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved all-in-one microcomputers could ship with BASIC and reach non-hobbyist buyers.
narrative.problemSolved: Early microcomputers were kits or bare boards; users needed a complete system out of the box.
